The Shift Is Here

AI agents don't assist shopping anymore. They complete it.

In January 2026, Google launched the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) — an open standard that allows AI systems to connect directly to a retailer's backend and complete transactions without sending users to a website.

Walmart, Target, Shopify, Visa, Mastercard, and dozens more have already signed on. This isn't a fringe experiment. It's industry consensus.

What This Means For You

If you're not agent-ready, you become invisible.

When an AI agent can complete a purchase from your competitor but not from you, market share migrates without an obvious cliff. It just... happens.

Checkout Without Clicks

AI agents browse inventory, check variants, apply discounts, and initiate payment — all without redirecting the user.

Real-Time Everything

Inventory accuracy, deterministic pricing, shipping timelines — agents need reliable data to complete transactions.

New Security Models

Non-human actors executing payments require fraud controls that don't block legitimate agent traffic.

Visibility = Conversion

In agentic commerce, appearing in AI results and completing the sale are the same question.

Our Approach

How we help you become agent-ready

The same learning-first process we use for product strategy, applied to the specific challenge of agentic commerce readiness.

1

Diagnose your current state

We deploy simulated AI shopping agents against your store to understand where carts break, checkout fails, or agents can't complete purchases.

2

Map the gaps

Real-time inventory accuracy? Deterministic pricing? Bot-friendly authentication? We identify exactly what's blocking agent-driven conversion.

3

Design the path forward

We help you prioritize fixes, design UCP-compatible flows, and plan integration with your existing commerce stack.

4

Build the capability

We work alongside your team to implement changes, test with real agent traffic, and leave you with the ability to evolve as the protocol matures.

Quick Assessment

Agent-readiness isn't a checkbox. It's a system.

Can you answer "yes" to all of these?

  • Real-time inventory accuracy across all channels
  • Pricing that doesn't change between browse and checkout
  • Payment handlers that work with non-human actors
  • Clear, machine-readable shipping commitments
  • Discount and loyalty logic that works without human input
  • Bot controls that don't block legitimate AI agents

Most commerce stacks have never been tested this way. That's where we come in.
